segments.script: Every surface you touch on your body — and every surface inside it — is covered by the same tissue type. What is it, and what makes it so effective?
segments.video_prompt: Animated cinematic cross-section of human skin surface. Camera zooms into the epidermis, resolving individual squamous epithelial cells — flat, tightly packed like hexagonal floor tiles. Golden-teal colour scheme, macro biology visual style.

segments.script: Epithelial tissue covers external, internal, and glandular surfaces. Four characteristics: avascular — no blood supply; minimal matrix — cells tightly packed; rests on a basement membrane; held by four junctions — tight junctions seal gaps, adherens junctions link actin, desmosomes anchor against pull, gap junctions allow ion exchange. Surfaces covered: 2 in acoelomates, 3 in pseudocoelomates, 4 in coelomates.
segments.video_prompt: Split panel infographic. Left side: body silhouette showing location labels for external (skin), internal (gut, lung), and glandular (thyroid) surfaces. Right side: a zoomed cross-section of epithelial cells on a basement membrane showing all four junction types as molecular callouts — tight (claudin rings), adherens (cadherin links), desmosome (intermediate filament anchors), gap (connexin channels). Clean scientific illustration, white background with blue-teal accents.
